name: Paul Simon
hook: A New York songwriter who went to Kingston to record reggae in 1971 and to Johannesburg to record with South African musicians in 1985, breaking a UN cultural boycott to make one of the best-selling albums of the decade.
blurb: Paul Simon was born in Newark, New Jersey, in 1941 and grew up in Queens, New York. With his school friend Art Garfunkel he formed Simon & Garfunkel, who recorded from 1964 to 1970, their later albums co-produced with the engineer Roy Halee. Their last, 'Bridge over Troubled Water' (1970), is one of the best-selling albums ever. Alone, he went to Kingston, Jamaica, in 1971 to record 'Mother and Child Reunion' at Dynamic Sounds, because Jimmy Cliff had recorded 'Vietnam' there, with Jamaican session players including Hux Brown, Jackie Jackson and Winston Grennan. When it reached the top five in America and Britain in 1972, it was one of the few records by anyone outside Jamaica to use reggae so prominently. 'Graceland' (August 1986) began with a bootleg cassette of South African mbaqanga music lent to him by the musician Heidi Berg. In February 1985 he went to Ovation Studios in Johannesburg to record with South African musicians including Ray Phiri, Bakithi Kumalo and Ladysmith Black Mambazo. South Africa was then ruled by apartheid, a system that kept Black people separate and without rights by law, and the United Nations had asked artists not to work there, so the trip broke that boycott. The African National Congress, the main movement fighting apartheid, protested, and Artists United Against Apartheid criticised him. The South African Black musicians' union had voted to let the sessions go ahead, and Simon paid the players about three times what top New York session players earned. He was put on the UN blacklist and taken off it in January 1987, and the UN Anti-Apartheid Committee later supported the album. People still argue about whether it was solidarity or a breach of a boycott that the people it was meant to help had asked for. Los Lobos have also said they were not credited for a track they say they wrote, which Simon disputes. He retired from touring in 2018 but has gone on releasing records.

signatureTracks.title: Mother and Child Reunion
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Recorded in Kingston with Jamaican session players: an American pop hit built on a reggae rhythm section.

signatureTracks.title: You Can Call Me Al
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The biggest single from 'Graceland', with Bakithi Kumalo's South African bass playing at the front of an American pop record.

signatureTracks.title: Homeless
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Written with Joseph Shabalala of Ladysmith Black Mambazo to a traditional Zulu wedding melody, and sung almost entirely by the group.
